disposition_mapping.rationale: Council converged (pragmatist, finance_domain, agentic_architect, hitl_designer, accounting_standards and emerging_economy on reflection) that due-item selection and proposal generation are already executed as one batch pass in real ERPs and no requirement protects PRE-01 as a standalone boundary. The merge is accepted only on condition the due-item list remains a separately logged, inspectable artefact and 'Approved matched invoices' remains the explicit leading input, preserving the KB-09/KB-11 evidence chain and satisfying PRE-R-01.

Proposal generation survives per PRE-R-08, fused into the same system execution as selection but still producing a distinct, named 'Payment proposal' output that T-02 subsequently inspects, so the review step is reviewing a real artefact, not an internal state of a black box.

A strong council majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards) rejected embedding review inside proposal generation as a 'continuous control layer,' holding that this collapses the control into the thing it checks and produces no demonstrable review artefact, which fails KB-05's error-correction requirement. Detection (duplicates, blocked vendors, bank-detail changes) is automated, but adjudication remains a distinct, separately evidenced human step, satisfying PRE-R-09, PRE-R-02 and PRE-R-03, with a manual fallback where the underlying change-log is not itself system-enforced.

The council's near-unanimous position (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards) against maximalist's threshold-based auto-approval is adopted: approval remains a live, individually-performed human act for every batch, bounded by delegation of authority, satisfying PRE-R-10. PRE-R-10's survival test is read as requiring the act, not merely a policy artefact a signatory periodically attests to. Actor separation from T-01 (PRE-R-04) is structurally preserved since the generating actor is never the approving signatory.

File generation is automated, but release is strengthened rather than loosened: a verification/hash-binding gate (agentic_architect, adopted by finance_domain and hitl_designer) blocks transmission unless the file matches the screened-and-approved record, and dual control applies above a value threshold with single-officer release below it to accommodate small finance units (emerging_economy's compromise, since a hard two-person rule is undeployable in a three-person back office). A manual/batch upload channel remains first-class alongside API transmission. PRE-R-05 (approval before release) and PRE-R-03 (review before release) are enforced as mechanical, not merely procedural, gates. PRE-R-11 is satisfied.

Unconstrained by design, so automation of the matching mechanics is adopted (finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, pragmatist). Against maximalist's and agentic_architect's round-1 absorption into a single execution megastep, the council (finance_domain, hitl_designer, accounting_standards) held that confirmation-matching must remain a distinct, nameable function because it is the event that fixes payable-derecognition timing (KB-11). Batch statement reconciliation is retained as a first-class, not degraded, alternative to API-based confirmation per emerging_economy, since several correspondent banks still issue end-of-day statements only.

Routine clearing and FX-difference computation are automated, but material or anomalous FX differences route to the GL accountant for a documented decision (finance_domain's materiality-threshold compromise, adopted by hitl_designer and accounting_standards), satisfying KB-04/KB-05's requirement for an accountable human on judgment-adjacent entries. PRE-R-06 and PRE-R-07 are preserved as hard, named inputs; KB-08 is satisfied because exchange differences are always posted as a separately identifiable line regardless of who or what posts them; KB-03 cutoff discipline is built explicitly into the posting logic per accounting_standards' and maximalist's concession.

Unconstrained by design and carrying no standards content of its own (accounting_standards), this is the council's clearest consensus candidate for near-full automation. Multi-channel delivery, including a non-digital fallback, is retained per emerging_economy to avoid a portal/email-only design that assumes universal vendor connectivity; the AP analyst is retained solely for delivery-failure exceptions.

steps.description: The ERP/automation selects approved, matched invoices due under their payment terms and, in the same batch pass, groups them by vendor, currency and payment method into a payment proposal. This consolidates what is operationally already a single system execution, but the due-item list and the proposal remain two separately logged, inspectable artefacts rather than one opaque transaction, preserving the invoice-to-GRN-to-PO evidence chain behind the payable. An AP analyst configures selection parameters and is the accountable reviewer of a visible exception queue: items excluded despite being due, disputed items, vendor-hold items, early-payment-discount decisions, and foreign-currency items near a rate-sensitive threshold. Data-quality anomalies (duplicate vendor IDs, missing currency codes, incomplete terms data) are surfaced explicitly, never silently normalised.
steps.name: Automated due-item selection and payment proposal generation

steps.description: A screening engine pre-computes duplicate-payment flags, blocked-vendor flags and vendor bank-detail-change flags against the payment history and bank master change log, presenting each flag with its underlying evidence rather than a pass/fail summary. The AP supervisor remains the accountable adjudicator of every flag (release, hold, escalate for out-of-band vendor verification), retained as a distinct, separately evidenced step rather than embedded inside proposal generation, because a control architecturally fused with the step it checks cannot produce a demonstrable 'this was reviewed, this is what was found' record. Where the underlying bank-detail change log is not itself a system-of-record (e.g. a manually maintained register), the step retains a manual log-review fallback rather than relying on automated pre-screening alone.
steps.name: Automated screening and proposal review

steps.description: The reviewed proposal, together with its flag evidence (not an aggregate total), is approved by an authorised signatory acting within delegated limits. Every batch requires a live, individually-performed human approval act; no sub-threshold or risk-tiered auto-approval is introduced, because approval is a liability-bearing act whose error cost (an unauthorised payment transmitted) is categorically different from, and not offset by, the convenience of automating routine cases. The signatory may be assisted by a risk-annotated summary, but the underlying reviewed proposal and flags must remain visible to them.
steps.name: Payment approval

steps.description: The approved proposal is converted into a bank payment file, whose generation is automated. Release to the bank is gated by a verification check, channel-agnostic (cryptographic hash-binding where systems support it; a locked proposal ID and manual verification checklist where they do not) confirming the transmitted file corresponds exactly to the record that cleared screening and approval, with no intervening vendor bank-detail change. Above a defined value threshold, release additionally requires dual control (a second treasury officer or equivalent maker-checker action); below threshold, a single treasury officer may release under system-enforced, time-separated logging, accommodating finance units too small to staff a permanent second release role. A manual/batch file-upload path remains a first-class alternative to API-based transmission, not a degraded fallback.
steps.name: Payment file generation and controlled release

steps.description: Settlement confirmations are matched to the transmitted payment file automatically where real-time or near-real-time bank connectivity (API, camt.054/MT942 feeds) is available; where it is not, end-of-day batch statement reconciliation remains an equally supported, first-class operating mode rather than a legacy exception path, since several correspondent and smaller domestic banks do not issue real-time confirmations. Unmatched, rejected or partially settled items route to a treasury-officer-owned exception queue carrying full context (original instruction, bank response code), kept as a distinct, nameable function because it is the specific event that makes payable-derecognition timing determinable.
steps.name: Bank settlement confirmation and reconciliation

steps.description: Routine clearing of AP subledger open items and cash posting to the GL are automated once settlement is confirmed, consuming the bank settlement confirmation and the settlement-date exchange rate as hard inputs. Exchange differences are always posted as a separately identifiable line, never netted into cash or AP clearing. Differences exceeding a documented materiality threshold, or arising from an anomalous or stale rate source, route to the GL accountant for a documented decision rather than auto-posting. Postings respect period-cutoff discipline: settlement events are posted into the period in which settlement actually occurred, with a defined, documented treatment for confirmations that arrive late relative to a period cutoff.
steps.name: Posting, clearing and FX settlement-difference recognition

steps.description: Remittance advice is generated and distributed to vendors automatically on settlement confirmation, via email, vendor portal, or a non-digital channel (SMS, printed advice) where a vendor lacks reliable digital contact data. The AP analyst's role is limited to the exception queue: delivery failures, bounced addresses and vendor queries. This function carries no accounting-standards content of its own and is the lowest-risk candidate for near-full automation in the workflow.
steps.name: Automated remittance distribution
